annotatedSteps.description: State the Right-Hand Thumb Rule and describe how it determines the magnetic field direction
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Right-hand thumb rule: Imagine that you are holding a current-carrying straight conductor in your right hand such that the thumb points towards the direction of current. Then your fingers will wrap around the conductor in the direction of the field lines of the magnetic field.
So if we know the direction of current, the curled fingers give us the direction of the magnetic field lines (concentric circles) around the wire.

annotatedSteps.description: Explain how the magnetic field changes with distance from the conductor
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: The strength of the magnetic field produced by a given current in the conductor decreases as the distance from it increases (it is inversely proportional to distance, B ∝ 1/r).
